payload.name: Broad-period temporal retrieval
payload.description: When a question names a calendar period (e.g., mid-August 2023, early 2023, last month) and asks what someone did, joined, or attended, use a time-range or unfiltered search instead of a single point target_time.
content: When a question specifies a period such as 'mid-August', 'early 2023', or 'last month', do not set time_mode to a single point target_time; use a time range covering the full named span, or omit the time filter and filter results manually by world_start.

If the first search used a restrictive point time and returned no relevant evidence, run an additional search without that point time or with a broader window before concluding 'no information available'.
Treat memories whose world_start falls within the named period as relevant even if the memory describes the event with relative phrasing like 'a few days ago' rather than an explicit date.

solves: This solves cases where a temporal question names a period (like mid-August or early 2023) but the agent converts it to a single point date, filtering out relevant memories whose start date falls later in that period and then wrongly answering that no information exists. The fix is to search with a broad time range or no point-in-time filter, then judge relevance by whether the memory's world_start falls inside the named period. Applies to any future retrieval question about events, classes, trips, or plans anchored to a vague calendar period.
